memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Then the LORD said to Moses, 'Write this on a scroll as something to be
remembered and make sure that Joshua hears it, because I will completely blot
out the name of Amalek from under heaven.'" - Ex 17:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a hard verse and it deserves honesty rather than a quick pass.

God pronounces judgment on Amalek. Deuteronomy 25:17-18 gives the reason: they
attacked the exhausted stragglers at the back, the weakest people in the column,
and they "had no fear of God." This was not a border dispute. It was predatory
cruelty against the defenceless.

We should not pretend this verse is comfortable. Divine judgment on a nation is
sobering, and Scripture does not soften it for us. But notice that it is
judgment, not arbitrary hostility. God is responding to what Amalek did to the
helpless.

Notice also the timescale. This judgment unfolded over centuries, not days. God's
patience is long even when His verdict is settled.

We must be careful here. This was a specific judgment on a specific nation in
redemptive history, spoken by God Himself. It is not a template for how God's
people treat enemies today. Jesus is explicit: "Love your enemies and pray for
those who persecute you" (Matt 5:44).

What remains for us is this: God sees what is done to the weak, and He does not
forget it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does it comfort or unsettle you that God takes cruelty to the weak seriously?
2. How do you treat those who cannot repay or defend themselves?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You see what is done to the defenceless. Give me a heart that protects the
weak, and help me to love even those who oppose me. Amen.
